text:
kevin: Heads-up — planning to cut over denormalized telemetry writes into the new timeseries store tomorrow 10:00 PT. Rough plan: dualwrite -> full backfill -> shadow reads for console -> flip. Need to align on quota window behavior and dashboard mappings.

anya: Can you share the exact gating checks for canary? Also want to confirm retention semantics for timeseries vs denorm. :eyes:

kevin: Canary checks: 1) error rate < 0.1% across write path for 30m, 2) console p95 query latency no worse than +30% for canary tenants, 3) match counts for prefix keys within 0.1% vs denorm for sampled tenants. If any fail, rollback dualwrite. Retention: timeseries will maintain raw per-minute buckets 90 days, then aggregated to hourly for 365d.

sam: Dashboard concern — we have a bunch of saved queries in Console that rely on the denorm shape (route_attrs nested JSON). Do we have a mapping plan so existing tiles don't break when we shadow-read?

kevin: Yes. Two-part approach: (A) query adapter layer in console that rewrites older saved queries to the timeseries shape for read-only paths, incremental mappings in a config table; (B) quickfail fallback to denorm read when an adapter rule misses. We'll run the adapter in canary first.

daphne: Backfill plan: we will run streaming backfill for last 30d then batch job for older windows. Estimated runtime: streaming ~ 6h for 30d at current throughput, batch ~ 12h for >30d. Backfill SQL snippet (for reference):

```sql
INSERT INTO timeseries.events_minute (ts_min, route_id, metric, value)
SELECT date_trunc('minute', created_at) as ts_min, route_id, 'requests' as metric, count(*)
FROM denorm.events
WHERE created_at >= now() - interval '90 days'
GROUP BY 1,2;
```

kevin: We'll run the backfill in a limited concurrency worker pool (max 8) and throttle by ingest QPS to avoid overload.

anya: Quota windows: currently we use a per-route daily window anchored at UTC midnight. For timeseries reads we can keep that but quota exposure (console) needs to show per-window consumed vs allocated. Who owns the UI mapping for that?

sam: That's me. For the display, I need a consistent series: window_start, window_end, consumed, limit. If the timeseries stores per-minute, we can roll up on the fly for console queries. We should expose an API that returns the rollup so I don't have to recompute client-side.

daphne: Also calling out SLAs: Dedicated customers expect no more than 1% change in billing metrics after cutover. We need a billing reconciliation run against last 7 days post-flip.

kevin: Agreed — add billing-smoke to the canary checklist: reconcile invoices for a sample cohort.

ingest-bot: Job scheduled: denorm->timeseries backfill kickoff at 2024-03-15T02:00Z (job-id: backfill-174880). Concurrency=4.

kevin: Quick manual rollback plan: stop dualwrite (config flip), route reads back to denorm read adapter, cancel backfill tasks, and open incident channel. Try to avoid schema-level destructive ops until 2w after stable.

anya: One more: monitoring. We need an end-to-end trace that verifies attribute parity for a sampled set of route_ids. I'll bake a quickcheck that compares top-10 metrics for sample tenant every 10m and alerts on >0.5% diff.

sam: +1 on alert. Also, when we flip, can we tag the first 48h of timeseries writes with meta:cutover=early so we can filter in dashboards?

daphne: Yes, add header x-cutover-phase on writes. We can strip later.

kevin: Ok team — action items:
- anya: write the canary gating doc and quickcheck (ETA end of day)
- sam: implement rollout-api for rollup endpoint and add dashboard mapping config (ETA tomorrow morning)
- daphne: finalize backfill worker config and billing-reconciliation job (ETA today EOD)
- infra: set backfill concurrency to 4 and throttles ready (pinged infra)

kevin: If no objections, we'll start dualwrite at 10:00 PT tomorrow. Post here any blockers. :thumbsup:
